title: Performance regression with FA2 and long-context generation after 5.2.0
author: andreasgoulas

comments.author: zucchini-nlp
comments.body: will take a look tomorrow, can confirm there is a small diff (I got ~200sec and ~190sec on avg per release tag)

comments.author: vasqu
comments.body:
#46696 is the wrong fix but it still might have found the underlying perf regression(?), just as a heads up

We might need to cache the compiled state

comments.author: zucchini-nlp
comments.body: Looks like it was caused by https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/42435. @vasqu could you take a look, checking out to the commit before that PR brings back the performance

comments.author: vasqu
comments.body: Yea lemme check what happened. Feel like the is_tracing call is too expensive it seems

comments.author: andreasgoulas
comments.body: @vasqu It seems that patching `is_tracing` in import_utils.py to always return False does not significantly impact the generation latency (tested on 5.4.0). So, this is probably not the root cause.

comments.author: andreasgoulas
comments.body: According to my measurements, `flash_varlen_fn` is significantly more expensive on 5.4.0 vs 5.2.0 (240us vs 140us - excluding the kwargs preparation code). This is quite strange since the inputs and the flash-attn implementation should be identical across the two versions. @vasqu

comments.author: vasqu
comments.body: This is indeed super weird, the tracing call was just my intuition tbh. I haven't had time to properly investigate yet sadly, if you revert the flash attention stuff in the forward, do we still get the same perf then?

comments.author: vasqu
comments.body: So revert the PR only for checking kwargs and the associated main forward

comments.author: andreasgoulas
comments.body: @vasqu After reverting the PR line-by-line, I think I found the root cause: removing the `.item()` call from max_seqlen_in_batch in `_get_unpad_data` somehow causes the next `_index_first_axis` calls to trigger this performance regression. It is not clear to me how this is possible - it could be the case that there is a memory leak or a hidden memcpy. A straightforward fix would be to re-introduce the `item()` call there, but I think that this issue requires a more careful investigation.

comments.author: vasqu
comments.body:
Ok wow that is really unexpected 😮 if you add a .item call before calling the index fn, everything is fine? Is there any difference between native FA2 and kernels FA2? `uv pip install kernels`

Because the native FA2 fn and the kernels ones should be slightly different

comments.author: andreasgoulas
comments.body: Yes, adding `max_seqlen_in_batch_k = max_seqlen_in_batch_k.item()` before the 2 index calls resolves the issue, at least on an NVIDIA RTX 6000 PRO. I also tested an RTX 4090 but the performance gap was not that significant there. ~Installing kernels==0.14.1 did not significantly affect the measured latency.~ @vasqu

comments.author: andreasgoulas
comments.body: Using the FA2 implementation from kernels, I can observe a small performance gain but the performance regression is still there.

comments.author: vasqu
comments.body:
That's super weird. So it seems to be GPU specific? I'm not sure whether it makes sense as general fix then, i.e. always call .item as it does have its own repercussions 😓 We can at least open a draft PR if you are open to it @andreasgoulas

@zucchini-nlp you also measured the latency, which GPU did you use?

comments.author: zucchini-nlp
comments.body: I check on the dgx with kernels FA, @vasqu

comments.author: andreasgoulas
comments.body: Yes, I will submit a draft PR reverting this specific change. I wouldn't say it is GPU-specific, but depending on the GPU the effect may be  more or less significant.

comments.author: andreasgoulas
comments.body: @vasqu I have submitted a PR that fixes this particular issue. Applying this patch on 5.4.0 fixes the regression completely. However, the timings on the latest version differ and, therefore, I marked it as draft while I investigate.

comments.author: vasqu
comments.body: Awesome, thanks a lot for all your detailed work on this, really appreciate it!

comments.author: ammmanism
comments.body:
@andreasgoulas @vasqu @zucchini-nlp – first of all, huge thanks for the deep debugging work here. The bisection down to the `.item()` removal in `_get_unpad_data` is a fantastic catch, and the draft PR (#47134) already proves the primary fix works on RTX 6000 Pro.

However, as @andreasgoulas  pointed out, timings on `main` **still** differ from the 5.2.0 baseline even with that patch applied – meaning there’s at least one secondary contributor stacked on top.

I have a clear roadmap to get this issue **fully resolved and safely merged**, and I’d like to take ownership of it:

### My immediate action plan if assigned:

1. **Validate the primary fix thoroughly**  
   - Run the `.item()` re‑addition across multiple GPUs (RTX 6000 Pro, RTX 4090, A100) to confirm parity with 5.2.0.  
   - Measure the exact overhead introduced by the device‑tensor path vs. Python scalar.

2. **Deep‑profile the root mechanism** (don’t just revert blindly)  
   - Use `torch.profiler` / `nsys` to compare both paths.  
   - Pinpoint whether the regression comes from:
     - a different kernel dispatch path inside `_index_first_axis` / `index_select`,  
     - repeated implicit synchronisations, or  
     - async kernel queue build‑up.  
   - Document the findings in the PR so future refactors don’t reintroduce the same trap.

3. **Hunt down the residual perf delta** (the unfinished business)  
   - With the `.item()` fix applied, bisect the remaining commits between 5.2.0 and current `main` that touch `modeling_flash_attention_utils.py` and the cache classes.  
   - Prime suspects: other removed `.item()`/`.cpu()` calls in the same refactor (#42435), or subtle changes to the `kwargs`‑building path for the FA2 call – the reporter already ruled out `is_tracing`, but I’ll systematically verify.

4. **Make the fix safe for `torch.compile` / graph capture**  
   - The original removal in #42435 was likely motivated by avoiding host‑device syncs under compilation.  
   - I’ll guard the `.item()` call with `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` so we get the performance fix in eager mode without breaking compiled graphs.

5. **Add a regression benchmark**  
   - Add a long‑context FA2 latency smoke test (or at least a documented perf script) to prevent this from regressing again – ideally gated in CI or added to the manual perf‑check docs.

I’ve already reviewed #47134 and #46696 (closed) to avoid duplication. I’m confident I can move #47134 out of draft, fix the remaining regression, and land this properly.

**Could one of you please assign this issue to me?** I’ll start by pushing an updated version of #47134 with the `compile`‑safe guard and the profiling results attached.

Looking forward to closing this one out
